articles.title: Liga U: el futuro del baloncesto español se podrá ver gratis en DAZN
articles.standfirst: La plataforma incorpora a su parrilla de contenidos desde este viernes la competición organizada por la ACB y la FEB y sólo bastará con registrarse con un correo electrónico
articles.summary: La plataforma incorpora a su parrilla de contenidos desde este viernes la competición organizada por la ACB y la FEB y sólo bastará con registrarse con un correo electrónico
articles.body: DAZN incorpora a su parrilla de contenidos la competición organizada por la ACB y la Federación Española de Baloncesto. Las retransmisiones arrancarán este viernes 23 de octubre con uno de los grandes encuentros de la competición, el Clásico entre Real Madrid y Barça Atlètic. Todos los encuentros estarán disponibles gratis en DAZN, sin necesidad de contratar un plan de pago, solo con registrarse con un correo electrónico. DAZN, la plataforma global de entretenimiento deportivo, ha alcanzado un acuerdo con la Asociación de Clubes de Baloncesto (ACB) y la Federación Española de Baloncesto (FEB) para incorporar a su oferta de contenidos la Liga U, la competición que reúne a algunas de las principales promesas del baloncesto español. Gracias a este acuerdo, los aficionados podrán disfrutar gratis en DAZN de más de 150 partidos de la temporada 2026/27, incluyendo toda la fase regular y la Final a 6, en la que se decidirá el campeón de esta edición. Para acceder a los encuentros, únicamente será necesario registrarse en la plataforma con una dirección de correo electrónico, sin necesidad de contratar una suscripción de pago. Las retransmisiones comenzarán este mismo viernes 23 de octubre, a partir de las 17:00 h, con uno de los encuentros más esperados de la temporada: el Clásico entre Real Madrid y Barça Atlètic. Ambos conjuntos volverán a verse las caras después de disputar la final de la primera edición de la competición, en la que el equipo blanco se proclamó campeón. Este enfrentamiento supondrá el punto de partida de una cobertura que permitirá seguir la evolución de los jóvenes talentos del baloncesto nacional a lo largo de toda la temporada. Con esta incorporación, DAZN continúa ampliando su oferta de baloncesto en España y refuerza su compromiso por acercar el deporte a todos los aficionados. La disponibilidad gratuita de la Liga U permitirá que cualquier usuario registrado en la plataforma pueda seguir la competición sin coste, contribuyendo a dar una mayor visibilidad a los jóvenes jugadores y facilitando que nuevos públicos descubran a las futuras estrellas del baloncesto español. La Liga U es una competición impulsada conjuntamente por la ACB y la FEB, con el apoyo del Consejo Superior de Deportes (CSD), que nació en 2025 con el objetivo de fomentar el desarrollo de los jóvenes jugadores y facilitar su transición hacia el baloncesto profesional. El proyecto combina una competición de alto nivel con un modelo que favorece la formación académica de los deportistas, permitiéndoles compaginar su evolución deportiva con sus estudios. En su segunda temporada, la Liga U cuenta con 14 equipos distribuidos en dos grupos: Real Madrid, Barça Atlètic, Burgos Grupo de Santiago, Casademont Zaragoza, Fundación CB Canarias, Valencia Basket y Bàsquet Girona integran el Grupo A, mientras que Kids&Us Manresa, Joventut Badalona, Amara Lleida, Euskaltax Bilbao Basket, UCAM Murcia CAR, Unicaja Alhaurín de la Torre y Obradoiro forman el Grupo B. La competición se desarrolla en distintas fases que permiten a los equipos enfrentarse a rivales de un nivel competitivo similar, favoreciendo así el crecimiento y la progresión de los jugadores. La temporada culminará con la Final a 6, que se celebrará del 13 al 16 de mayo de 2027 y reunirá a los seis equipos clasificados para disputar el título. DAZN ofrecerá íntegramente esta fase decisiva, en la que se conocerá al nuevo campeón de la Liga U. La Liga U presenta a muchos de los grandes talentos del futuro del baloncesto español, con nombres que dan que hablar cada semana como Mohammed Dabone (Barça Atlètic), Omer Kutluay (Real Madrid), Diego Niebla (Joventut Badalona), Lucas Marí (Valencia Basket) o Pau Torrens (Amara Lleida), entre muchos otros. En apenas un año de historia de la competición, casi medio centenar de jugadores de la Liga U han saltado ya a la pista en la Liga Endesa.

articles.title: Dream reportedly sell out 17,000-seat NBA arena ahead of Game 3 of WNBA Finals
articles.summary: Dream fans are showing major support for the team ahead of Game 3 of the WNBA Finals.
articles.body:
A last-minute arena change for the WNBA Finals proved to be a wise decision by the league. The Atlanta Dream reportedly sold out the 17,000-seat State Farm Arena for Game 3 just a week after the league announced the game would be played there , according to Front Office Sports.

While the Dream had played previous playoff rounds at State Farm Arena, the WNBA Finals were initially scheduled to occur at the same time other events were happening at the stadium. Because of that, Game 3 and Game 4 of the WNBA Finals were originally scheduled to be played at Gateway Center, where the Dream usually play. Gateway Center sits just 3,500 fans, the lowest figure in the league.

To get around that, the WNBA altered its schedule for Game 3 and Game 4 of the Finals, moving Game 3 up one day and altering the time of Game 4 so that the Dream could play both games at State Farm Arena.

The league announced that change Oct. 13. Just over a week later, the Dream reportedly sold out the arena. It's a significant development for the team, as its previous playoff games at State Farm arena reportedly averaged fewer than 10,000 fans per game, according to FOS.

The league has not announced its plans for a possible Game 6. If the series is still going at that point, Atlanta would host another home game. Game 6 of the WNBA Finals is currently scheduled for Thursday, Oct. 29 at 8:00 p.m. ET. That's the same time the Atlanta Hawks — who play all their home games at State Farm Arena — are slated to take on the Cleveland Cavaliers that day.

If the series goes to a Game 6, the WNBA will likely look to move the date of the game or start it earlier in the day to allow both teams to play at State Farm.

That's a very real possibility considering how the series has played out thus far. After dropping Game 1 to the Golden State Valkyries, the Dream took Game 2 thanks to a dominant performance by Angel Reese .

The series is tied 1-1 heading into Game 3, which will take place Wednesday.

articles.title: Steve Kerr Makes Candid Admission About Warriors' Failed LeBron James Pursuit in NBA Free Agency
articles.summary: Even though the Golden State Warriors were believed to be among the teams LeBron James had interest in joining as a free agent this summer, head coach Steve Kerr doesn't believe they ever got close to an agreement.
articles.body:
Even though the Golden State Warriors were believed to be among the teams LeBron James had interest in joining as a free agent this summer, head coach Steve Kerr doesn't believe they ever got close to an agreement.

Speaking to The Ringer's Logan Murdock , Kerr explained the pursuit of James "never went wrong" because it was "never really that close" to begin with:

"It never went wrong. We were never really that close. Steph and Dray obviously are friends with him, so they were doing the recruiting. I know LeBron now pretty well from the Olympics, and so I reached out to him during free agency and he's always really good about responding to texts. He's one of the guys who you text, you get a response. I just said, 'Hey, if we have something to chat about, let me know.' And I never heard back. And I wasn't offended at all.

"So while all this chatter was going on, like 'LeBron's going to Golden State,' I'm like, 'No, he's not.' We've worked together, we have great respect for each other. If he was interested, he would not just be talking to Steph and Dray, but he'd reach out and we'd have discussions. In the end, I think he made the right decision. It's a team that he gets to go to as the new guy, but also a team that hasn't won a title in 40-plus years. And can you imagine seeing him in a Warriors uniform? It would have been so weird."

The discussion about James to the Warriors really peaked when Draymond Green turned down his $27.7 million player option, giving the front office some flexibility to add free agents.

Golden State's pitch to James would have been centered around the opportunity to play alongside Stephen Curry after the two showed incredible on-court chemistry with Team USA during the 2024 Olympics.

After helping the U.S. win gold in Paris, James described playing with Curry as "everything and more."

The Warriors' roster talent was not at the same level as some of the other top suitors for James, including the Philadelphia 76ers, Miami Heat and Cleveland Cavaliers.

Curry, Green (who presumably would have signed a new deal with a lower 2026-27 salary to remain with Golden State) and Brandin Podziemski are the top three players for the Warriors. Jimmy Butler's recovery from a torn ACL is expected to have him back on the court around January or February.

Even with all of those players healthy, though, James would likely have had to shoulder a lot of the burden on both ends of the floor that he may not be physically capable with his 42nd birthday approaching on Dec. 30.

Curry already had an injury scare during the Warriors' open practice on Sunday, though Kerr told reporters his star guard is doing fine and will play in the opener against the Lakers.

James chose the 76ers to join a roster that already had Jaylen Brown, Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and VJ Edgecombe. It's a strong mix of established veterans and still-rising young players to take some of the pressure away from him.

Green returned to the Warriors by signing a one-year deal worth the same $27.7 million he originally opted out of after James' decision.

As much fun as it would have been for fans to see James and Curry play in the NBA together, Kerr certainly didn't sound like he was ever preparing for it to become a reality.

Instead, fans will have to wait until the March 24 when the Warriors host the 76ers to get the first matchup between Curry and James this season.

articles.title: Angel Reese, Dream vs. Valkyries Game 1 Makes WNBA History with Record TV Viewership Numbers
articles.summary: The Golden State Valkyries' 68-64 win over the Atlanta Dream set a WNBA Finals viewership record.
articles.body:
The Golden State Valkyries' 68-64 win over the Atlanta Dream set a WNBA Finals viewership record.

Game 1 last Saturday averaged 2.1 million viewers across NBC and Peacock, the largest-ever rating for a WNBA Finals opener. The broadcast peaked at three million as the Valkyries sealed their victory.

Not surprisingly, San Francisco (4.49 million) had the largest viewership in terms of individual markets. New Orleans was next on the list at 3.04 million.

Golden State held on to win what proved to be a defensive struggle. The Valkyries and Dream combined to shoot 32.4 percent from the field and commit 22 turnovers.

Gabby Williams (26 points) was the only Golden State player to score in double figures. On the other side, Angel Reese posted what was then her second double-double (14 points, 12 rebounds) of the postseason.

The Dream evened up the series in Game 2 with an outstanding performance from Reese. She scored 30 points and hauled in 16 points as her team won by 14 points. Jordin Canada matched her double-double by putting up 13 points and 10 assists.

Game 3 is Wednesday in Atlanta with tip-off at 8 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Lakers' Season 'Hinges on Walker Kessler,' NBA Scout Says Ahead of Debut with Luka Doncic
articles.summary: Even though Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves are the faces of the Los Angeles Lakers, the feeling among people around the NBA is the team's ceiling will depend on their biggest offseason acquisition.
articles.body:
Even though Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves are the faces of the Los Angeles Lakers, the feeling among people around the NBA is the team's ceiling will depend on their biggest offseason acquisition.

One Western Conference scout told The Athletic's Dan Woike ahead of the Lakers' season-opening game against the Golden State Warriors that their season "hinges on Walker Kessler" being the player they anticipate:

"Their season hinges on Walker Kessler," the scout said. "One, he has to be healthy. And then two, he has to be good. … And because he hasn't played in a competitive NBA game, we don't know how he's going to handle that."

Every NBA Team's Top 3 Trade Targets This Season 🎯

One area in which the Lakers will need Kessler to show his dominance is on defense because of how the roster is constructed, particularly with Dončić and Reaves being players opposing teams frequently target.

Speaking to ESPN's Dave McMenamin , Lakers head coach JJ Redick said he believes Kessler has the "potential" to be one of the best rim-protecting centers in the NBA.

"I think Walker has the potential to be one of the best rim [protection] guys, and when he's played, he's been that for the most part. ... So, it's more just being excited about this team, than comparing the two teams."

There is tremendous pressure on Kessler given how much the Lakers paid to get him in a sign-and-trade with the Utah Jazz. They sent two unprotected first-round picks and two pick swaps, then signed Kessler to a four-year, $130 million contract.

One reason the Lakers spent so much in both money and draft capital on Kessler was to appease Dončić.

According to McMenamin, Dončić gave the front office feedback on how he wanted them to fill out the roster and one of the items was an "A-list center" to play alongside.

When the Lakers arrived at training camp in September, Dončić specifically said he "really wanted" Kessler in Los Angeles.

It remains to be seen if Kessler is capable of being the A-list center that Dončić requested. The 25-year-old didn't get a chance to show much last season because he only played five games for the Jazz due to a torn labrum that required surgery.

Kessler hasn't played more than 64 games in a season since his rookie year in 2022-23. Some of that can be attributed to the Jazz not trying to win many games late in seasons after falling out of playoff contention, but now he is coming back from a major injury.

When Kessler does play, he puts up defensive numbers that rank among some of the best players in the NBA.

Since his rookie year, among players with at least 500 shots defended, he is third in opponent field-goal percentage (54.6) in the restricted area as the closest defender. Chet Holmgren and Victor Wembanyama are the only players ahead of him in that category.

Kessler ranks second in blocks per game since the start of the 2022-23 season. His offense figures to get a boost playing with Dončić, who has had success throughout his career creating easy buckets for centers.

Daniel Gafford had the best stretch of his career after being acquired by the Dallas Mavericks midway through the 2023-24 season to help them reach the NBA Finals.

The Lakers are locked in with Dončić, Reaves and Kessler as their primary trio for the foreseeable future. They will make at least $120 million combined in each of the next two seasons.

If Kessler hits in the way the Lakers are banking on, they could vault into being part of the top-tier Western Conference teams with the San Antonio Spurs and Oklahoma City Thunder.

articles.title: Luka Doncic Writes Letter to Lakers Fans, Eyes 'Run For a Championship' Ahead of NBA Opener
articles.summary: Luka Dončić is promising fans the Los Angeles Lakers will be competing for a title in the franchise's first season since parting ways with LeBron James.
articles.body:
Luka Dončić is promising fans the Los Angeles Lakers will be competing for a title in the franchise's first season since parting ways with LeBron James.

Dončić addressed Lakers fans in an ad published in Wednesday's edition of the Los Angeles Times (h/t The Athletic's Dan Woike).

"Dear LA, tonight we start our run for a championship," Dončić's letter began.

Dončić continued, "We have a special team. We know what you expect, and we are going to do everything in our power to deliver it.

"From the moment I arrived in LA, you welcomed me with open arms. That is something I will never forget. So here is my promise to you: we are going to give you everything we have, every single night."

Dončić and the Lakers are set to open the 2026-27 season Wednesday night against Stephen Curry and the visiting Golden State Warriors.

This isn't the first time Dončić has expressed hope he will be playing for a title next spring. He said during training camp earlier this month he feels the Lakers "can be a championship team" in 2027.

Dončić is set to make his season debut Wednesday alongside a new-look starting lineup for the Lakers. Austin Reaves is returning as a starter.

The rest of the starting five will be rounded out by newcomers in Walker Kessler alongside some combination of Ziaire Williams, Matisse Thybulle and Quentin Grimes.

The Lakers started Dončić, Reaves, Kessler, Williams and Thybulle in last Friday's preseason finale against the Denver Nuggets.

Lakers fans haven't seen Dončić play since April 2, when he suffered a hamstring injury that ultimately kept him out of the entirety of his team's run to the second round.

Dončić, who led the NBA with 33.5 points per game last season, will be tasked in his return not just with providing offensive production but in taking over as the new face of the Lakers franchise.

The Lakers star led a trip to Slovenia this offseason that was attended by every teammate excepting rookie Cameron Carr, per The Athletic's Dan Woike .

That team bonding trip and the open letter to fans could be signs Dončić is ready to step into the leadership role left open by James, who made his Philadelphia 76ers debut in a Tuesday night win over the defending champion New York Knicks.

The Lakers are set to begin their own season Wednesday night with a 10 p.m. ET tip-off at Crypto.com Arena.

articles.title: Pedro Martínez: "No es fácil adaptarse a jugar y producir menos a cambio de que el equipo sea mejor"
articles.standfirst: El entrenador del Real Madrid habla sobre el reparto de minutos de su plantilla antes de visitar al Maccabi Tel Aviv en Belgrado
articles.summary: El entrenador del Real Madrid habla sobre el reparto de minutos de su plantilla antes de visitar al Maccabi Tel Aviv en Belgrado
articles.body: Pedro Martínez, entrenador del Real Madrid, consideró que el nivel de la NBA "es más alto" que el de la Euroliga en la que juega su equipo durante la rueda de prensa previa al encuentro de la máxima competición continental en el que deberán medirse a domicilio al Maccabi de Tel Aviv. "Con sus connotaciones y con sus reglamentaciones, pero en la NBA son mejores, tienen mejores jugadores, tienen mejores entrenadores y el nivel de la NBA es más alto que el de la Euroliga. Aunque sí que es verdad que la Euroliga es una grandísima competición, están los mejores jugadores de Europa y jugadores muy buenos que vienen de Estados Unidos", dijo. "Hay equipos que juegan muy bien en Europa, como también hay equipos que juegan muy bien en la NBA. Son 30 franquicias de la NBA, son 18 en la Euroliga, y hay equipos que juegan bien y hay equipos que no juegan tan bien en los dos sitios. Máximo respeto y admiración por el baloncesto de la NBA y por los entrenadores de la NBA en general", añadió. Martínez afirma que afrontan en choque "animados" sabiendo de las dificultades de medirse a un equipo donde muchos jugadores llevan mucho tiempo jugando juntos con el mismo entrenador. A ello han ayudado los últimos encuentros, donde se han ido a muchos puntos. "Estamos preparados y también entrenamos para partidos que van a ser de otro tipo, en los que nos vamos a encontrar otras dificultades, en los que se va a jugar a otro ritmo, en los que en seguramente vamos a estar menos a gusto, porque ahora ya estamos más a gusto en este tipo de ritmo. No siempre vamos a jugar a marcadores por encima de 100 puntos. Y no quiere decir ni que no vayamos a ganar ni que no vayamos a jugar bien", señaló. "Yo creo que ahora mismo la tendencia que hay clarísimamente en la ACB y también en Europa es ir a posesiones cortas, buscar la ventaja rápido, jugar con una intensidad alta. Es un tipo de baloncesto en el que me siento a gusto, pero no hay una manera única de jugar bien a baloncesto, todas son buenas dependiendo de los jugadores y de lo bien que lo hagan los equipos", opinó. El entrenador defendió la importancia de repartir tiempo en pista: "Todos los jugadores que tenemos, si jugaran más minutos, harían mejores estadísticas. Y se están adaptando por el bien del equipo a jugar menos minutos y, por lo tanto, a producir menos a cambio de que el equipo sea mejor. Es un proceso, y no es un proceso fácil". "En otros equipos que he estado no ha salido bien porque hay jugadores que no se adaptan, porque no están acostumbrados, porque a lo mejor priorizan más sus números individuales que los del equipo. A unos les está costando más que a otros. No voy a poner nombres, pero ya se ve. Mientras tengan buena mentalidad... para mí lo importante es el equipo y para los jugadores lo importante es su actuación porque es la que depende de ellos", agregó. Uno de los que menos está participando es Max Shulga, a quien descarta ceder: "¿Si se nos lesiona un jugador en la posición de 1-2? Entonces, ¿qué hacemos? ¿Fichamos un jugador de fuera o le damos ahí minutos a Max Shulga que conocerá nuestra forma de jugar, que el chico está trabajando bien en el día a día? Veremos qué va pasando durante la temporada, no lo sabemos. A lo mejor no tenemos lesiones, improbable. Preferimos tener un equipo largo y no quejarnos cuando haya lesiones". "Yo como entrenador no puedo estar pendiente de si un jugador juega mucho o poco. Mi responsabilidad es con todo el equipo. Intento que todos estén con confianza, que todos se sientan importantes y ya veremos cómo va la temporada. Estoy contento con Max Shulga, de tenerlo en el equipo, de cómo está entrenando. A día de hoy no está teniendo minutos, pero es una decisión mía, soy yo responsable de ella, pero no tiene nada que ver ni en la calidad del jugador, ni en la mentalidad del jugador, ni en el trabajo en el día a día. Y esto yo ya se lo he dicho a él, él lo sabe", expresó. En cuanto a Nick Smith Jr., manifestó: "Está haciendo muy bien en los entrenos y yo creo que va a ir a más. Viene de un baloncesto diferente. Aquí el reglamento es diferente, se entrena diferente, se juega diferente... él está en el proceso. Tampoco podemos obviar una realidad de que nosotros somos una plantilla en la que todos los jugadores son muy buenos. Tiene una gran competencia en su puesto y él está un poco por detrás que ellos porque tiene menos bagaje. Pero la temporada es muy larga, estamos en el mes de octubre", completó.

articles.title: 76ers' Joel Embiid Says Injuries Made Him 'Miserable' and 'Depressed,' 'Hated Coming Into the Gym'
articles.summary: After winning the 2023 NBA MVP award, Philadelphia 76ers star center Joel Embiid has endured three straight injury-riddled seasons.
articles.body:
After winning the 2023 NBA MVP award, Philadelphia 76ers star center Joel Embiid has endured three straight injury-riddled seasons.

Embiid opened up to The Athletic's David Aldridge about the mental toll the last few years have taken on him, and he said he's bringing a more positive mindset to the 2026-27 campaign.

"I went through a period the last few years, obviously, I've come down with injuries," Embiid said. "I just hated coming into the gym. Like, injuries, I can't play, this and that. I was miserable, and depressed. I just thought that's the biggest thing we need — that, not necessarily joyful personality, but something else. And I'm a grown man. A lot of it is on me to fight through it. But then again, it's also nice when you have other people around you that felt that way and can boost you up a little bit."

Embiid had 13 points and 11 rebounds in Tuesday night's season-opening 106-100 win over the New York Knicks.

With experienced former champions like LeBron James, Jaylen Brown and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope added to the roster, Embiid appears more willing to defer to his teammates as he tries to achieve his ultimate goal of winning a title.

"I think the biggest thing that someone like 'Bron adds, other than being LeBron James, is just championship mentality. I feel like I know what it takes to win, but I haven't done it," he said. "I'm looking for guidance on, like, what am I doing wrong? I want to learn a little bit more. Like, I feel like I know a lot, but then again, I'm still willing to learn. All these years, I haven't really had that championship mentality around me. So it's like, what can I do better?"

Embiid and the Sixers will be back in action on Thursday night against the Cleveland Cavaliers.

articles.title: NBA stays silent on WNBA Finals teams skipping the national anthem before Games 1 and 2
articles.summary: The NBA has not answered OutKick’s questions about the Dream and Valkyries’ WNBA Finals anthem absences despite a rulebook requirement to stand in line.
articles.body: The Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries left the court for the national anthem before the first two games of the WNBA Finals, despite a provision in the league’s own rulebook calling for players to stand and line up during the performance. Now the NBA has joined the WNBA and both teams in leaving OutKick’s questions about those absences unanswered. DREAM, VALKYRIES SKIP NATIONAL ANTHEM IN WNBA FINALS GAME 2 DESPITE RULEBOOK REQUIREMENT OutKick contacted NBA Executive Vice President and Chief Communications Officer Mike Bass on Tuesday. The inquiry asked about the NBA’s role in the matter, possible discipline and whether the teams would be instructed to be present for the anthem before Wednesday’s Game 3. The NBA did not respond by the deadline. The WNBA and both teams also have not answered OutKick’s repeated inquiries. NBA asked about its role in WNBA anthem enforcement The WNBA’s 2026 official rulebook calls for players, coaches and trainers to stand and line up along the sidelines or foul line during the national anthem. OutKick asked Bass whether the NBA has a role in overseeing or enforcing that provision, or whether enforcement is solely the WNBA’s responsibility. We also asked whether NBA Commissioner Adam Silver or anyone at the NBA league office had discussed the absences with WNBA leadership and, if so, what guidance had been provided. WNBA SILENT AS FINALS TEAMS SKIP NATIONAL ANTHEM DESPITE RULE REQUIRING PLAYERS TO STAND IN LINE Additional questions covered whether either team had received an exemption, whether discipline was planned or under consideration, and whether the teams would be instructed to be on the court for Game 3. The NBA was given until the end of Tuesday to respond. Bass’s responsibilities span both leagues. His 2026 Sports PR Summit biography says he oversees public relations, including basketball and business communications, for the NBA and WNBA, among other leagues. The NBA’s involvement in the WNBA dates to its creation: the NBA Board of Governors approved the women’s league in 1996. Bass previously issued an NBA statement on anthem policy In February 2021, Bass issued an official NBA statement reiterating the league’s requirement that teams play the national anthem. The statement said "all teams will play the national anthem in keeping with longstanding league policy." That statement addressed playing the anthem. OutKick’s current questions concern whether WNBA teams must be on the court during the performance. Before Saturday’s WNBA Finals opener and Monday’s Game 2, both teams left the floor ahead of the anthem and returned within seconds of the performance ending. OutKick contacted the WNBA, Dream and Valkyries after Game 1 and followed up with all three Sunday, asking about the absences, the league’s anthem requirements and plans for Game 2. After both teams were absent again Monday, OutKick followed up with all three Tuesday, seeking explanations and asking about plans for Game 3. OutKick attended five pregame and postgame press conferences Saturday, plus both coaches’ pregame and postgame press conferences Monday. OutKick was not called on to ask a question at any of the nine sessions. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD The WNBA has a written provision calling for players to be on the floor for the anthem, but its Finals teams have twice been absent. Asked about it, the NBA has been just as quiet as the WNBA.

articles.title: 76ers' Joel Embiid Asks LeBron 'What Can I Do Better?' and Wants to Learn 'Championship Mentality'
articles.summary: Joel Embiid discussed how LeBron James' championship mindset can help the star center achieve more playoff success as the duo begins their shared tenure on the Philadelphia 76ers.
articles.body:
Joel Embiid discussed how LeBron James' championship mindset can help the star center achieve more playoff success as the duo begins their shared tenure on the Philadelphia 76ers.

"I think the main thing is not necessarily about vets; it's where we're trying to go," Embiid told David Aldridge of The Athletic. "I think the biggest thing that someone like 'Bron adds, other than being LeBron James, is just championship mentality. I feel like I know what it takes to win, but I haven't done it. I'm looking for guidance on, like, what am I doing wrong? I want to learn a little bit more. Like, I feel like I know a lot, but then again, I'm still willing to learn. All these years, I haven't really had that championship mentality around me. So it's like, what can I do better?"

James signed a two-year contract to join the 76ers as a free agent on July 24, continuing a busy offseason in which the team previously acquired five-time All-Star Jaylen Brown in a blockbuster trade with the Boston Celtics.

Philadelphia added plenty of experience by bringing in James, as the 41-year-old has captured four championships and made 10 NBA Finals appearances throughout his stellar career.

James has scored 8,521 total points in the playoffs, while no other player in NBA history has crossed the 6,000-point threshold in the postseason.

He'll look to help a 76ers squad attempting to contend for the Eastern Conference crown.

Embiid has established himself as an elite offensive force since joining Philadelphia in 2014, racking up seven All-Star nods, five All-NBA selections, two scoring titles and one MVP award.

The 76ers have failed to make an Eastern Conference Finals appearance in all eight of his playoff runs, though.

Embiid and James helped Philadelphia secure an impressive win over the New York Knicks to begin its 2026-27 campaign on Tuesday night, taking down the defending champions by the final score of 106-100.

articles.title: Jeremy Fears Jr., Thomas Haugh Headline 2026 AP Preseason All-America Team
articles.summary: The 2026-27 college basketball season is just over a week away, and the top players entering this year have been identified.
articles.body:
The 2026-27 college basketball season is just over a week away, and the top players entering this year have been identified.

The Associated Press released its preseason All-America team, led by Michigan State guard Jeremy Fears Jr. and Florida forward Thomas Haugh, who were near-unanimous selections from the 58-person media panel. The full team is as follows:

Jeremy Fears Jr., G, Michigan State (57 votes)

Fears is coming off a stellar redshirt sophomore season in which he averaged 15.2 points and a nation-leading 9.4 assists per game. While he likely would've been a first-round NBA draft pick, he returned to school in hopes of leading Michigan State to its first national championship in 27 years.

"I think we have the pieces," Fears said. "We've kind of got a lot of everything, and my job is to get them the ball."

Haugh helped Florida win the 2025 national title and led the Gators with 17.1 points per game last season on his way to earning third-team AP All-America honors. He also likely would've been a 2026 first-round draft pick, but he wanted to add a second national title to his resume.

"It's national championship or bust for this team," Haugh said. "But we're mature enough. We have a really old group now, so I think we're going to be really comfortable coming in this season."

Tanner also earned third-team AP All-America honors after averaging 19.5 points and 5.1 assists. Mirkovic averaged 13.3 points, a team-high 8.0 rebounds and 2.6 assists for an Illinois team that reached the Final Four for the first time since 2005. Krivas averaged 10.4 points and a team-leading 8.2 rebounds to help lead Arizona to its first Final Four run in 25 years.

It will be exciting to see if these players live up to expectations and which other players emerge as top talents throughout the upcoming season.

articles.title: Fantasy Basketball: Paul George delivers vintage performance, plus more takeaways from 2026-27 NBA Opening Night
articles.summary: Fantasy basketball analyst Dan Titus breaks down Opening Night's triple-header.
articles.body:
The 2026-27 NBA season tipped off with a bang, giving us a three-game slate that began in the afternoon with a classic Eastern Conference matchup and concluded with a battle between two juggernauts in the Western Conference.

In between, we caught a glimpse of what the Sixers could be, and how hard it'll be for the Knicks to repeat as champs.

Here are my fantasy basketball takeaways from NBA Opening Night.

Celtics: Jayson Tatum struggled; PG held it down

Paul George scored 38 points (12-21 FG, 7-8 FT) with 5 rebounds and 3 assists in just 31 minutes. He also hit 7 3s and had 5 steals, totaling 60.5 fantasy points. Dominant on both ends, George couldn't have had a better debut for Boston. That 35% usage rate is unsustainable and speaks to how reliant the C's were on George on opening night.

Jayson Tatum went the other way, shooting 6-of-23 (0-of-7 from 3) for 13 points, but he still had 11 assists, 4 rebounds and 32 fantasy points. It's encouraging to see his usage was near 29%, and the shots will fall. He has a penchant for shooting contested jumpers — and won't let up on those — so low-efficiency nights will happen. He should get to the cup more, but either way, it's a prime buy-low spot for someone panicking, and you could argue it is a perfect sell-high opportunity for George.

Quick hits: Derrick White (17 points, 8 assists, 1 steal and 4 turnovers) and Payton Pritchard (17 points with 4 rebounds in 27 minutes) both had solid outings, not great ones. Both guards were passive, given that Tatum and George accounted for 55% of Boston's shot attempts. Still, I'm not concerned about either of their fantasy values.

Duncan Robinson (21 points with 5 3s) and Javonte Green (19 points off the bench, plus-21) helped the Pistons rally back from 22 points in a comeback win over the Celtics.

Jalen Duren scored 22 points on 8-of-13 shooting and grabbed 9 rebounds with a 2 stocks in just 28 minutes. He was a force all game and is showing no signs of rust despite missing most of the preseason in a contract standoff. Cade Cunningham finished with 22 points, 4 rebounds and 8 assists and 2 stocks. Three of Cade's eight dimes went to Duren, showing that this elite duo hasn't missed a beat. Cunningham had 5 turnovers, which will always hamper his 9-cat status, but 40 fantasy points and 39 from Duren are still good numbers.

Quick hits: Ausar Thompson stuffed the stat sheet with 11 points, 11 rebounds and 5 assists and 1 steal in 33 minutes. He also made all three of his free-throw attempts. W.

John Collins was underwhelming in 25 minutes, scoring 6 points, grabbing 5 rebounds with a steal. It was good to see him get backup center minutes behind Duren, though.

Waiver guys: I'd consider Duncan Robinson for Sunday's matchup against the Sixers if you need 3s and points to win. It's a seven-game slate, the third-lowest of the week.

76ers: Embiid played defense; Maxey is the 1A

Joel Embiid shot 4-of-15 but still got 13 points, 11 rebounds, 6 assists, 2 steals and 3 blocks, for 46.2 fantasy points. His defense carried his second-half performance, though he also took a reckless shot late, an all-too-familiar bonehead play. Hopefully he realizes he doesn't need to do that much: stay healthy, rebound, defend, don't flop and don't make bad business decisions.

Tyrese Maxey looked like the 1A, with 28 points, 5 assists, 3 steals and 3 blocks in 39 minutes, equating to 56.3 fantasy points. 6 stocks is ridiculous for a guard. Can't believe people were concerned about him. He also had the highest usage rate among the starters.

Quick hits: LeBron James had 14 points, 9 rebounds, 7 assists, 2 stocks and 1 turnover. Jaylen Brown balled out in 34 minutes, scoring 19 points, 8 rebounds, 6 assists and 2 stocks. VJ Edgecombe had 9 points on 4-of-10 in 34 minutes. I warned about his usage and opportunity, and the first game he looked like I expected. Ten shots won't cut it, and without an injury to the other four starters, nights like this will be common.

Waiver guys: Anfernee Simons? He scored 13 points with three 3s in 25 minutes. Since the Sixers play three more games this week (including a back-to-back) on the lightest slates, I would pick him up for scoring and 3s like Robinson.

Knicks: Brunson's burner wasn't lit on ring night

Jalen Brunson shot 6-of-19 (32 percent) and 1-of-3 from 3 for 21 points. He went 8-of-8 at the line, adding 5 rebounds, 3 assists, 2 turnovers, with no stocks in 34 minutes. His 29.5 fantasy points fell short of expectations, but his 28% usage rate held. Karl-Anthony Towns was efficient but was limited by foul trouble: 19 points on 6-of-9, 12 rebounds, 1 assist, 1 steal, 2 blocks and 4 turnovers in 24 minutes. No concerns from a fantasy perspective.

Quick hits: OG Anunoby had a rough shooting night, going for 10 points on 3-of-12 from the field and 1-for-9 from 3. Josh Hart had 14 points, 7 rebounds and 3 assists. Mikal Bridges had a forgettable game, with 4 points on 2-of-8 shooting with 3 boards and no stocks.

Waiver guys: Andre Drummond had 12 points and 14 rebounds, but don't trust it. KAT was in foul trouble, and when Drummond gets 13 shot attempts, it's probably good for the opposing team. If you're down on rebounds heading into Sunday, he's an option, but don't expect this level of output.

Oklahoma City Thunder and San Antonio Spurs

Thunder: SGA shines in Western Conference Finals rematch

Shai Gilgeous-Alexander looked like he was in mid-season mode, netting 32 points with 6 rebounds, 4 assists, 3 steals and 3 blocks in 36 minutes. He and Paul George were the only players to top 60 fantasy points on Tuesday night. His usage rate was 33%. Most impressively, he did it against the Spurs on just 4 free-throw attempts. Pretty flawless game for a consensus top-four fantasy pick.

Quick hits: Jalen Williams went 5-for-16 from the field for 12 points and 7 rebounds. He looked rusty in his first game back. Chet Holmgren had 14 points, 7 rebounds and 4 blocks. It was good to see him play 30 minutes; hopefully that sticks. Holmgren held up much better tonight than he did in Game 7 of last season's Western Conference Finals.

Waiver guys: Ajay Mitchell versus Cason Wallace: Mitchell won the first round in minutes and production, with 23 minutes, 5 rebounds and 6 assists to Wallace's 19 minutes and 6 points on 3-of-8. For now, keep them both rostered in 12-team leagues.

Aday Mara made highlight plays, blocking Wembanyama, running the floor and finishing an alley-oop. That said, he shouldn't be rostered in 12-team leagues unless Isaiah Hartenstein or Chet Holmgren gets hurt, because 12 minutes isn't enough, but his size and impact in limited minutes earned him a spot on the watch list.

Jared McCain, on the other hand, is worth scooping for points and 3s. He had 20 points with six 3s in 22 minutes. Plus, he'll play Thursday and Sunday, so he'll likely fit into your lineups.

Spurs: Wemby struggled, but still put numbers up

Victor Wembanyama shot an abysmal 1-of-13 from the field, scoring 12 points (10-12 FT) with 13 rebounds, 6 blocks and 3 assists, for 49.1 fantasy points. It was by far the worst shooting performance of his career. We won't see games like this often, so fantasy managers can expect a strong bounce-back on Friday.

Quick hits: San Antonio put De'Aaron Fox, Stephon Castle and Dylan Harper in the starting lineup, and all three guards produced. Castle led the way with 27 points on 9-of-21 (5-of-12 from three) with a surprising 35% usage rate. Fox had 14 points, 7 rebounds and 7 assists and a steal on 6-of-9 shooting, while Harper had 18 points, 7 rebounds and 5 assists. Each finished with 30-33 fantasy points.

Waiver guys: Julian Champagnie is a good short-term streamer. In 30 minutes, he scored 8 points with two 3s, but added an unexpected 3 blocks. He had 28 fantasy points in his debut and is rostered in 21% of leagues.

articles.title: NBA breakout candidates: 11 players who could surprise in a big way in 2026-27
articles.summary: Here are some players who could make a leap and impact their teams this season.
articles.body:
The NBA season is here! As competitive as it will be, there are always players who surprise. Breakouts can occur all over the league, but also at different levels. From a star to a superstar, from potential to consistent contributor. The leaps these players make can lift their teams in ways we can't always see in October. Here are the players I have in mind that could break out and impact their teams this season.

I would normally Eurostep a Year 2 prospect as a breakout candidate, but Harper's growth is too much to ignore. It was clear to see just how much Harper improved over the course of his rookie year, and how impactful that improvement from Harper was in the postseason. The moment has arrived now as he's worked his way into the Spurs' starting lineup.

The command he showcased last season allowed the Spurs to have consistent guard play. Imagine if that unlocks the Spurs' three-guard lineup at the start of the season? In the preseason, we saw a lack of hesitation — nothing new, but there was a determination behind it. The drives felt smoother, and he had no problem hitting first once he got in the paint. And if the defense gave him space in pick-and-roll, he went right to a stepback or a pull-up.

There was a loudness to the way McDaniels spoke about (and then performed against) the Denver Nuggets in the playoffs. Since then, Minnesota has shifted its identity to a smaller, younger and more athletic bunch — and it's easy to see a potential amplification on that noise from McDaniels this season.

His aggression has not stopped offensively, and that fits within what Minnesota wants to do: Get out and run in transition. A throw-ahead to McDaniels could get an easy bucket or get him attacking to a midrange shot. Depending on matchups, the Wolves can use McDaniels as a screener. There is room for him to be involved in more pick-and-roll and handoffs, and he's had zero issue reading the defense and being aggressive to look for his shot. The more he becomes a threat for Minnesota, the stronger the team will be. Plus, he will defend anybody .

It should not be forgotten how much Thompson grew as a player last season. The everlasting question seems to revolve around his jump shot, but what if he simply gets a lot better at the things he's already good at? And does the experience he's gained pay off this season with more guard play changing his context? Without having to initiate as much offensively, can that energy shift back to the defensive end?

If the ball-handling growth sticks, he can become an ever-present paint touch with his speed and athleticism. If teams are working to cut off those drives, perhaps he finds a comfort in accepting the space and mixing in pull-ups. That's on top of the excellent work he does as a cutter and the fact that Houston is playing a little faster, which could boost him in transition. If he can consistently make the defense pay, think about how that could elevate the Rockets' attack.

A lot of the conversation surrounding Detroit's offseason was about — drum roll — not adding playmaking to the room. There's been a thought bubbling in the back of my mind that whatever some may think the Pistons lack, the team believes it has in Ausar Thompson. There is a feel of improvement to his decision-making, ball-handling and passing. A comfort to run pick-and-roll and, whether it's a drop or a switch, attack that space, engage and work to pass out of it.

The ball in Thompson's hands unlocks the ability to move Cade Cunningham off flares or pindowns. There is also a growing comfort in driving to his spot and rising up if he's cut off. The Pistons work to move him around the board, but if teams want to put a big or a lesser defender on him, things open up. He can be used as a screener and a roller. The more he adds to the Pistons attack, the more they can keep pressure on teams.

There was a consistency that Miller showcased in the latter half of last season that the Hornets have to believe will stick around. The breakout feels less about the talent Miller has, but how he adds to it. There have been glimpses of more poise in the playmaking department.

The journey of every scorer is to navigate when that scoring draws more attention from defenses: noticing when there are two on the ball and getting off the ball; driving in the paint, seeing help come and spraying it to the perimeter; a greater understanding of knowing your job on that possession has been done. There is enough movement within what Charlotte wants to do offensively that he won't have to nail those, but it will make him and the team better. Understanding the shots he wants to take, driving and making plays could make him a different threat.

With the Thunder's roster changes, the runway is clear for Mitchell to continue to ascend. You have to think about Mitchell's skill set within what the Thunder like to do. A lot of the preseason chatter revolved around Shai Gilgeous-Alexander being moved off-ball, and a part of that is the trust Mitchell has earned in the OKC ecosphere.

His ability to drive and reject pick-and-rolls fits right in, and if he's drawing attention, think of the players he is kicking out to. Mitchell initiating action, running pick-and-roll and advancing to Jalen Williams or SGA is tough for a defense to handle. That's on top of dealing with an aggression and desire to score the ball whenever the opportunity presents itself. A world where defenses have to account for Mitchell opens a lot up for an (already great) Thunder team.

There is zero doubt that Murray-Boyles will continue to bring a level of havoc, disorder and disarray to opponents on the defensive end. There's an activity that consistently stands out. He's just always doing something on the defensive end of the floor. Quick hands, understanding and positioning erase whatever windows offenses think they have found.

The offensive growth is where he can really enhance his impact. His work at the 5 has been gold. Screening on- or off-ball opens him up as a roller to score or make decisions. He's got a knack for flashing into open areas and snaking around the dunker spot. If he continues to add drives and shows a confidence to take the 3s presented to him, the Raptors have a lot of lineups they can throw at teams.

The breakout case for Kessler is grounded in taking the things we've seen him do well and doing it night in and night out. The Lakers acquired him because of his ability to rotate to protect the rim, screen-and-roll and finish. If he does that consistently, the impact will be felt for a Lakers team that needs his production.

His ability to time his rotations around the rim to contest and block shots will boost what the Lakers want to do defensively. On offense, he'll have to work to develop chemistry with Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves to open up the pick-and-roll, making an effort to get to his roll quicker and become a short roll and lob threat. If he produces that for this specific team, the conversation around his ceiling may shift.

It's a combination of two teammates, but both feel set up for success in different ways. Eason is a reminder that success in this league is not always linear. He likely appeared as a breakout candidate last year, though the season wasn't as full as expected. But without his contract status hanging over his head, what could that mean for this season ?

His size and length open up lineup versatility for the Rockets. His growth offensively could impact the lineups the Rockets can throw out there. Being involved in more pass-and-cut actions in the half-court to get downhill is a different way to attack. Showcasing more confidence and patience with the ball in his hands is a plus for a Rockets offense that can run dry at times. Mixing in makes from 3s with the ability to beat closeouts and keep advantages is a win.

For Sheppard, the mission appears to be a lot simpler. Fred VanVleet and Marcus Smart are in tow, so the ask will be different. Instead of being the only pull-up threat for the Rockets and being tasked with mixing in playmaking, there's a world where he can be himself: more off-ball actions to unlock the pressure his shot-making can unlock; simplifying his reads in pick-and-roll because others will be able to initiate and make plays. He may not showcase the full radar of growth, but he might have an opportunity to double down on what he does well.

Yes, I can hear you through the screen, but stick with me. Mitchell has showcased a specific blend of on-ball commotion and a level of might on his drives. That's felt like a fit for what the Miami Heat (culture) wants. What does that look like with Giannis Antetokounmpo on the roster?

As opposed to relying on his drives to the level the Heat did last year, they might be a bonus. His ability to attack in transition combined with a willingness to beat closeouts could pop even more this season. Mixing in some catch-and-shoot 3s will help. If he's able to blend his speed with decision-making, we may walk away feeling differently about his overall impact for the Heat.

articles.title: Steve Kerr Teases Retirement Timeline, End of Warriors Dynasty with Steph Curry, Draymond Green
articles.summary: Steve Kerr signed a two-year extension to remain the head coach of the Golden State Warriors, but his long-term future may remain a subplot with the franchise in such a delicate position.
articles.body:
Steve Kerr signed a two-year extension to remain the head coach of the Golden State Warriors, but his long-term future may remain a subplot with the franchise in such a delicate position.

In an interview with The Ringer's Logan Murdock , Kerr was somewhat noncommittal about his status beyond his contract.

"I signed for two years and I can't see myself walking away after this year, but it feels now like there's some shape to this thing," he said. "There's some clarity. I could see this ending where [Stephen Curry], [Draymond Green], we all leave around the same time. I could see that happening."

Murdock responded that Kerr's remarks aren't dissimilar to what he said "two, three years ago," and he remains in the exact same place.

"I'm well aware that the NBA's crazy," Kerr said. "Anything could happen."

It's probably tough to walk away as long as Curry is a Warriors player. He and Kerr are connected in a way that few other NBA players and coaches are thanks to having worked for 13 years and won four titles together.

For Kerr, however, there's the stress that comes with trying to win a title when an organization's championship window might be closed altogether. Since its last Finals win in 2022, Golden State has twice reached the second round of the playoffs and twice missed the postseason altogether.

The Warriors' trajectory is unlikely to improve when they didn't make any big additions in the offseason, and a large part of their hopes rest on 37-year-old Jimmy Butler coming back strong from a torn ACL.

Kerr, Curry and Green all exiting the Bay Area at the same time would be fitting from a narrative perspective, but sports rarely provide for closure like that. Otherwise, Klay Thompson would still be a member of the Warriors.

Fans won't be too shocked if there's somebody different coaching the Warriors ahead of the 2028-29 season and maybe even before that.

articles.title: Duke, UNC, Kentucky Headline 'Tier 1' Schools Spending $20M+ on CBB Rosters, New CBS Report Says
articles.summary: After the costly failure that was the 2025-26 season, Kentucky is once again hopeful a massive NIL outlay will bring on-court success.
articles.body:
After the costly failure that was the 2025-26 season, Kentucky is once again hopeful a massive NIL outlay will bring on-court success.

According to CBS Sports' Matt Norlander and Isaac Trotter , the Wildcats are one of 11 schools in Tier 1 for spending in men's basketball. The others are Duke, Florida, Illinois, Louisville, Michigan, North Carolina, St. John's, Tennessee, Texas and Texas Tech.

Tier 1 is reserved for those with a budget of $20 million or more. A sign of how the financial landscape has shifted, Norlander and Trotter estimated that Kentucky and Louisville were the only schools that met that threshold last year.

Florida, for example, will have one of the most expensive rosters in the country after convincing Thomas Haugh, Rueben Chinyelu and Alex Condon to stick around in Gainesville. Haugh likely would've been a first-round pick in the 2026 NBA draft if he had declared.

"We definitely have a well-compensated team this year, but this is really the first year where we've been at the top, in terms of that conversation," Florida coach Todd Golden told CBS Sports. "... We're not going into the portal every year spending $20 million. We're retaining talent, guys that are growing within our program."

Michigan, meanwhile, was stuck between a rock and a hard place given the timing of Dusty May's exit.

The Wolverines already lost Morez Johnson Jr., Yaxel Lendeborg and Aday Mara as they try to defend their national title. They would've been in even bigger trouble if Elliot Cadeau or Trey McKenney had decided to explore their options after May left to coach the Dallas Mavericks.

North Carolina might be the most fascinating Tier 1 team given who it hired to replace Hubert Davis.

Michael Malone was an NBA Finals-winning coach with the Denver Nuggets in 2023, but he hasn't worked at the college level since 2001. Needless to say, the sport has evolved a lot since then.

Despite the Bill Belichick experiment being a disappointment for the football team, the Tar Heels are basically hoping a similar formula can make them successful on the hardwood.

articles.title: Steve Kerr’s Jimmy Butler Warriors injury update comes with Michael Jordan, Kobe Bryant comps
articles.summary: The Golden State Warriors are just hours away from kicking off their 2026-27 NBA season on Wednesday night vs the Los Angeles Lakers on the road. The Warrior...
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors are just hours away from kicking off their 2026-27 NBA season on Wednesday night vs the Los Angeles Lakers on the road. The Warriors will be without several key players in this one, including Jimmy Butler , who will miss a good chunk of this season as he recovers from a torn ACL he suffered a year ago.

Recently, Warriors head coach Steve Kerr gave the latest update on Butler's recovery process.

"He's doing great. I just talked to him this morning. He was in our weight room. He looks good. He feels good," he said, per Logan Murdock of The Ringer.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Kerr also spoke on the mentality that Butler brings to the Warriors when he's on the floor.

"He just has this aura about him, and it's a very unique trait. Michael Jordan had it, Kobe had it. I'm not just talking about physical dominance or skill dominance or how many points you score. I'm talking about an emotional hold on a game where everybody in the gym knows you're the man," he said.

Indeed, Butler has long been known for his strong personality both on and off the court, which has at times rubbed fans and teammates the wrong way, but has also yielded impressive results, with Butler dragging the Miami Heat to two NBA Finals appearances during his tenure there before burning that bridge.

The Warriors' tandem of Butler and Stephen Curry looked quite impressive during their brief time together dating back to 2025's trade with Miami, but unfortunately, injuries have derailed any chances of postseason success with the two so far.

In any case, the Warriors and Lakers are set to tip off on Wednesday at 10:00 pm ET from Los Angeles.

articles.title: Washington basketball guard gets fifth season approved in courts
articles.summary: Washington Huskies guard Tayshawn Comer found out after practice Tuesday that his fifth season of eligibility has been approved.
articles.body:
Washington's first basketball practice open to the media came with an extra surprise on Tuesday.

When practice wrapped, Nevada transfer Tayshawn Comer found out that he had received a temporary injunction in his legal case for a fifth season of eligibility, making him immediately eligible just before the season officially starts. Word spread quickly throughout the team, who had been meeting with their position groups, and the entire roster mobbed Comer in celebration.

A Huskies spokesman confirmed to the media after the scene that Comer had received his injunction, subject to NCAA appeal.

The decision comes as part of Glancey v. NCAA, which covers 76 college basketball players who graduated high school in 2022. Former Washington women's basketball guard Hannah Stines, who is in the transfer portal, is also among the players granted a year of eligibility by Tuesday's decision.

Comer played two seasons at Eastern Kentucky, one at Evansville, and one at Nevada before transferring to Washington, which had a roster spot open because the program learned that Croatian national Boris Tišma was not going to win his bid for NCAA eligibility. (Tišma later signed with Movistar Estudiantes of Primera FEB, the second division of Spanish basketball.) He averaged 11 points and 3.6 assists per game in 36 starts for Nevada last season and had been working as one of Washington's primary ball-handlers in the practice open to media Tuesday.

"I've been taking it day by day, just focusing on the season," Comer said after practice. "I really haven't been thinking about the eligibility. I knew it was out of my hands. Just leave it up to my lawyer and let him do what he has to do."

"I had a few options hitting the portal for my fifth year, but talking with Coach (Danny) Sprinkle, talking to Coach (DeAndre Haynes), he recruited me at Marquette. But once he got here, he started recruiting me, and we just built from there," Comer said when asked what made him choose Washington.

Comer started Washington's exhibition against Boise State and led the team in minutes with 33:45 of court time. He and Texas Tech transfer LeJuan Watts led the team in scoring with 16 each, 10 of which came on free throws from Comer. He also had 3 assists, 1 rebound, and made both of his threes while operating the offense.

Comer's injunction means the Huskies will have their full 15-man roster available for an exhibition against Washington State on Sunday and their season opener against Colgate on November 2. Only San Francisco transfer Ryan Beasley and walk-on BJ Roy did not play against Boise State, which means the Huskies are in good health coming into the season as well, after struggling with injuries last season.

articles.title: Atlanta Dream Sell Out State Farm Arena For WNBA Finals Game 3
articles.summary: The Atlanta Dream sold out State Farm Arena for Game 3 against the Golden State Valkyries. Angel Reese led the charge with 30 points and 16 rebounds.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Dream just proved they own the city. Tickets for Wednesday night's WNBA Finals Game 3 at State Farm Arena are completely gone, according to WSB-TV. This isn't just a win for the box office; it is a massive shift in the local sports culture. Channel 2 sports director Zach Klein received confirmation from the team regarding the sellout, which represents a distinct triumph for the franchise. Fans are paying top dollar to see Angel Reese and her teammates take on the Golden State Valkyries at 8 p.m. The only tickets left are on the secondary market, where prices have skyrocketed.

Resale prices show just how much demand has exploded. Ticketmaster lists seats from $91 to over $330, while SeatGeek has some going for as much as $1,300, per WSB-TV. Stubhub ranges from $89 to $271, and TickPick shows listings up to $1,400. These numbers tell a simple story: Atlanta is ready to embrace this team. Collaboration between the Dream, the Atlanta Hawks, and the NBA facilitated shifting the contests from the Gateway Center to the primary arena. This deal ensures the Dream will call State Farm Arena home for all their games starting in 2027.

The energy in Atlanta stems directly from the team's recent performance. Monday night saw the Dream secure their inaugural WNBA Finals victory in the history of the franchise. Angel Reese led the charge with a dominant stat line of 30 points and 16 rebounds in Game 2, according to Yahoo Sports . Her mindset after that win was clear and intense. "I was hungry. I wanted one and we let one slip away and you can't do that, especially on the road," Reese said. That drive is exactly what fans are paying to see live.

Reese also noted the team's emotional shift after a tough loss. She explained, "This is a good environment and a good team. We all came together and we were pissed. We felt disappointed. We felt embarrassed, and we didn't like the outcome of that last game." This raw honesty connects with the crowd. The series is currently tied 1-1, setting up a critical battle for home-court advantage. The Dream need to win here to keep the momentum rolling.

This sellout changes the landscape for women's sports in Georgia. State Farm Arena will host Game 3 and Game 4 by the Dream, following an agreement reached between the Dream, WNBA, Atlanta Hawks, and NBA. Saturday at 1 p.m. marks the tip-off for Game 4, while the Hawks adjusted their home opener to 8:30 p.m. to accommodate the schedule. This coordination shows the league is serious about growing the sport in this market. The move from the smaller venue to the big stage signals a permanent upgrade for the franchise.

Atlanta fans have shown they will fill the seats if the product is right. The Dream have capitalized on this by bringing the finals back to the heart of the city. With Reese playing at an elite level and the crowd fully engaged, the pressure is now on the Golden State Valkyries.

articles.title: Kristaps Porziņģis reportedly dealing with recurring POTS symptoms as Warriors explore trade options
articles.summary: Porziņģis was first diagnosed with POTS in 2025.
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors are exploring trade options involving forward Kristaps Porziņģis, ESPN's Shams Charania reports .

Porziņģis has been away from the team while dealing with recurring POTS (Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome) symptoms.

Last week, the Warriors forward posted on social media about his health.

"Hello people, I'm working with doctors and experts to figure out how to be fully back to good health asap," the one-time All-Star and NBA champion wrote . "Honestly, I'm getting better and better. I just have to stay patient, and I believe I'll be feeling great again soon. It has definitely been frustrating dealing with some health stuff that you can't exactly pinpoint, on top of injuries throughout my career, so it has added up for sure, but we will get through it. Health is wealth. Thank you for all the support."

"I appreciate all the internet doctors trying to diagnose and help, but I'm in the best hands. So everyone can relax now … and I don't have hiv or aids."

On October 14, before Porziņģis released his statement, Golden State said the forward would remain "out indefinitely" and, at the time, called it a "health-related" matter.

Charania's report on Wednesday was the first time that it was said to be recurring POTS symptoms. Porziņģis was first diagnosed with POTS in 2025.

According to Cleveland Clinic , "POTS is a condition that causes your heart to beat faster than normal when you go from sitting or lying down to standing up." Symptoms can vary widely from patient to patient, but Porziņģis' seem more respiratory and fatigue-related.

POTS significantly limited the 7-foot-2 Porziņģis during an Eastern Conference semifinal series against the New York Knicks in the 2024-25 season, when he was still with the Boston Celtics.

Porziņģis averaged just 15.5 minutes in that six-game series, which ended Boston's NBA title defense, with Celtics head coach Joe Mazzulla revealing after Game 5 that Porziņģis didn't play the second half because " he couldn't breathe ."

articles.title: Austin Reaves Explains Why Lakers Fans 'Probably Hated' LeBron James Before He Signed with LA
articles.summary: LeBron James was never quite revered in Los Angeles in the same way as other Lakers legends like Kobe Bryant. But Austin Reaves offered his thoughts on the matter, specifically the comparison between James and Bryant.
articles.body:
LeBron James was never quite revered in Los Angeles in the same way as other Lakers legends like Kobe Bryant. But Austin Reaves offered his thoughts on the matter, specifically the comparison between James and Bryant.

"I think with the Bron situation it was a little different just because Bron and Kobe were battling for the best player in the NBA for multiple years, so Lakers fans at the time probably hated LeBron," he told Melissa Rohlin of the California Post . "Not that they didn't accept him when he was here, but they still probably had the 'Kobe is better' type of mentality. But they don't have that with Luka [Dončić]. He was kind of after Kobe. They don't have a reason not to embrace him like a Kobe or someone else who was a Laker legend."

The Lakers certainly embraced Luka Dončić this summer, making it abundantly clear that they were building the franchise around him for the foreseeable future by letting James walk in free agency and adding players who fit their star's playing style.

Those new-look Lakers will make their 2026-27 regular-season debut on Wednesday night against the Golden State Warriors with a revamped starting five featuring Reaves, Doncic and Walker Kessler.
